$comment: Bio prose written by Claude from facts Fatima supplied and from her own personal study essay, at her request to rewrite rather than quote. Every factual claim here traces to something she said or wrote. Flagged for her correction.
intro: I am an artist from Doha working mainly in textiles, print and Arabic letterforms.
paragraphs: Most of what I make begins with a question about communication, and specifically the kinds that do not use words. Gesture, rhythm, repetition, pattern. The way an object left on a table implies a person who was there a moment ago. The way a symbol carries meaning long before anyone stops to explain it.

That interest took me toward Islamic and Ottoman decorative traditions, where meaning is carried by pattern rather than by picture, and toward Arabic calligraphy, where a letter can be read or simply looked at. I have spent a long time on the construction methods behind Persian illumination, the Rumi and Hatayi motifs and the flower forms built up from numbered geometry, because understanding how the pattern is made changes what you can say with it.

In practice this means my work tends to accumulate. A piece usually starts as a print and then keeps going: dye, stitch, quilting, paint, and calligraphy over the top of all of it, until the surface holds several processes at once. I am more interested in a surface that has been worked than one that has been resolved.

I am starting a Psychology degree in September 2026. It sounds like a departure from the art, and it is not. Both are the same question from different directions: how people understand each other, and what happens in the gap between what is meant and what is received.
note: Written from what Fatima has told Claude so far. She has been asked to correct anything that is not hers.
